answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can force each new identity to bond capital and wait through a delayed harvest of attested work, much like an orchard that only pays after seasons of visible labor. A nebula of throwaway accounts then becomes expensive: every clone must post the same lock and survive peer countersignature windows. When a fake cluster is later slashed, the loss ripple hits every bonded identity in that cluster, so an attacker cannot cheaply flood governance with disposable votes.
